- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00–0.20), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- In periods with high sentiment (e.g., >0.20), model frequently underestimates downside risk; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for each sentiment >0.20.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80.00), model tends to ignore it; apply smoothing or decay filter to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; use 18-day rolling average as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, avoid linear extrapolation; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×sentiment + 0.3×history).
